blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers hold approximately 69% of the world's freshwater supply.
They play a direct role in controlling global sea levels.
Glacial melt feeds vital Asian rivers including the Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra.
Glaciers actively regulate global climate through their high albedo.
Glaciers account for roughly 69% of global freshwater storage.
High albedo of glaciers reflects sunlight, making them essential for climate regulation.
Glacial source of major river basins: Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra.
